plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large golden flower heads that track the sun when young. Widely cultivated for seeds, oil and ornamental use, it thrives in full sun and is at peak bloom in mid-summer across the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September)
plants.location: North America, Europe, and temperate Asia; native to the Americas
plants.funFact: The flower head is actually made up of hundreds to thousands of tiny individual florets arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and spikes of fragrant purple flowers. Late-blooming plantings in cool-summer regions are still colorful in August, attracting bees and butterflies.
plants.location: Mediterranean region, southern France, England, Pacific Northwest, and Tasmania
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and its name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large, round leaves held above water and spectacular, fragrant blossoms rising on tall stalks. It blooms profusely during the warm monsoon and summer months in shallow ponds and lakes.
plants.location: India, China, Japan, Southeast Asia, and northern Australia
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a micro-textured surface that repels water and dirt, a phenomenon known as the 'lotus effect' that inspires self-cleaning materials.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with the largest flower head of the protea family, featuring a bowl of pointed pink bracts around a center of fuzzy florets. It flowers in the Southern Hemisphere's late winter and spring, beginning around August.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (August to November, peaking later)
plants.location: Fynbos region of South Africa's Western and Eastern Cape
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of South Africa, and its lineage is ancient, with protea relatives dating back to when Gondwana was still intact.
